learning_outcomes.text: To be able to understand Newton's Laws
To be able to use Newton's Laws for solving physics and engineering problems
To be able to use Work, Energy and Momentum conservation laws.
Ability to design and conduct experiments, gather data, analyze and interpret results for investigating engineering problems.
Ability to work efficiently in intra-disciplinary and multi-disciplinary teams; ability to work individually.

syllabus_topics: Measurement, introduction to physical quantities and vectors.
Vector representation using component and unit vectors. Basic vector operations. Scalar and vector multiplication of vectors.
Motion and its representation; position, velocity, acceleration. Average and instantaneous quantities and their calculations.
Movement in one dimension and two dimensions.
Properties of friction force; static and kinetic friction coefficients.
Solving for motion of objects using forces; free-body diagrams.
Force and work, kinetic energy, and the work-energy theorem.
Applications of work and energy concepts.
Conservation of energy and its applications
Momentum, collisions and conservation of momentum.
assessment_rules: The final success grade is determined by a 40% contribution from the Midterm Examination and a 60% contribution from the Final Examination.
bibliography: Raymond A. Serway ve John W. Jewett, Physics for Scientists and Engineers with Modern Physics, 10th edition, Cengage, 2019. ISBN: 978-1-337-55329-2
